newsitem.title: FRANCE: Vallourec sees Mannesmann venture positive.
newsitem.headline: Vallourec sees Mannesmann venture positive.

text.p: French steel firm Vallourec said on Tuesday it expects its planned joint venture with Mannesmann to have beneficial effects on 1998 results and to be "highly positive" from 1999, despite restructuring costs.

"In 1998, startup and restructuring costs will be lower than the expected benefits. But it will be from 1999 that the impact will be very positive on the results," chairman Jean-Claude Cabre told a news conference.
The company is aiming for a gross operating profit of 10 percent of turnover, he said.
"This merger was necessary to make our upstream activities more competitive. It will allow us to rationalise production and investment," Cabre said.
He added that a remaining 6.7 percent equity stake and 11.8 percent of voting rights held by Usinor-Sacilor in Voullourec represented a "purely financial interest."

Vallourec said on Monday it would form a joint venture with Mannesmannrohren-Werke to make unwelded stainless steel. The venture could be running by mid-1997 at the earliest and the start of 1998 at the latest, if approved by the European Commission.
The merger will lead to the closure of three Mannesmann rolled steel mills in Germany, two at Krefeld and one at Bous.
Vallourec will transfer 3.9 billion francs of annual turnover to the new company, while Mannesmann will endow it with 5.2 billion francs.
Vallourec had 1995 turnover of 7.6 billion francs, while Mannesmannrohren-Werke reported 23 billion francs. Usinor is selling 21 percent of its 27.7 percent holding to Mannesmann as part of the deal.
